issues.description: Constructor signature for StockIngredient is inconsistent across artifacts: the problem statement's UML specifies a 3-parameter constructor StockIngredient(String, int, int), the solution implements a 3-parameter constructor, but the template repository provides only a 4-parameter constructor StockIngredient(String, int, int, boolean). This mismatch will confuse students (the UML/statement and solution expect a 3-arg constructor) and may cause compile errors when students follow the specification or the solution examples.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor signatures consistent. Recommended fixes: (a) In the template, add a 3-argument constructor StockIngredient(String name, int price, int quantity) that delegates to the existing constructor (e.g., call the 4-arg constructor with a default strictValidation value), or (b) update the template's constructor to the 3-arg form used in the UML and solution. This preserves the intended design and prevents compilation/usage confusion.

issues.description: Constructor signature mismatch for StockIngredient: the problem statement (and the solution) describe a three-argument constructor StockIngredient(String, int, int), but the template repository only provides a four-argument constructor StockIngredient(String, int, int, boolean). This discrepancy can confuse students about which constructor to use/implement and how to instantiate StockIngredient as required by the exercise.
issues.suggestedFix: Add a public three-argument constructor StockIngredient(String name, int price, int quantity) to the template (or overload the existing constructor). For example, implement: public StockIngredient(String name, int price, int quantity) { this(name, price, quantity, false); } so the template matches the problem statement and the solution signature.
